Lina (eng-runtime): Quick heads-up — since yesterday ~18:00 UTC we've been seeing intermittent p95 spikes on long-context inference (seq lengths 20k-40k). Spikes line up with heavy KV eviction churn when FIFO path is active.

Lina (eng-runtime): snippet from node logs around spike:
```
[2026-03-16T18:07:12Z] kv: evict start id=0x7f8a reused=true reason=paging
[2026-03-16T18:07:12Z] kv: page_swap start pages=12 target=50
[2026-03-16T18:07:12Z] runtime: fallback to generic kernel due to cache-pressure=true
[2026-03-16T18:07:12Z] request 0xabc p95=420ms (prev baseline 60ms)
```

Owen (eng-runtime): Do we have a simple repro? sounds like reinsert/race with FIFO cooldown might be triggering pager churn + kernel fallback. Any batching/kernel selection changes around that time?

Lina (eng-runtime): Repro is noisy but attached a small harness that hits a 32k seq with many concurrent queries (concurrency=40) and short prefix reuse. Flags: `kv_eviction_policy=FIFO`, `kv_cooldown_ms=5_000`, `kv_prefetch=false`. Command we used: `./bench --seq 32000 --conc 40 --prefix-ratio 0.1`. pprof-ish top shows spikes in `kv_pager::scan` and `kernel::emit_unoptimized`.

Maya (eng-runtime): FIFO wins on steady throughput but terrible when a small hot set keeps getting reinserted right after eviction. LRU would keep hot keys, but LRU's metadata overhead can fragment slabs under extreme paging patterns. Could we try increasing `kv_cooldown_ms` to 30s as a quick mitigation? :thinking:

Raj (eng-sre): No OOMs reported, but host RSS jumps ~1.8x during spike window then slowly returns. Interesting line: kernel selection falls back to slower path when page swaps > 8/s which matches the timing. Could be a sharp latency/CPU combo rather than pure memory.

DeployBot: Deployed `kv_eviction_policy=FIFO` as default in release 2149999999 (canary 2149999999-2). Change log: "optimize steady-state eviction for lower avg cost".

Owen (eng-runtime): Short-term mitigations: 1) bump `kv_cooldown_ms` to 30k for any instance serving long contexts; 2) enable `kv_hot_prefix_cache` for prefix-heavy workloads; 3) add metrics: `kv_eviction_reinserts`, `kv_page_swaps`, `kv_fragmentation_pct`, and instrument kernel fallback reasons.

Lina (eng-runtime): Ran a quick A/B on a small canary: baseline (FIFO, cd=5s) vs canary (FIFO, cd=30s). Results across ~10k requests: baseline p95=410ms, canary p95=95ms; CPU tail reduced by ~40%. So cooldown helped in this workload.

Maya (eng-runtime): That matches hypothesis — reinsert thrash gives the pager oscillation which trips kernel fallback. Longer-term: introduce per-key sampled hotness counter + sampled LFU bias so we don't reinsert immediately after eviction. Also ensure eviction + reinsert is ordered atomically so rescanning doesn't see half-evicted state.

Raj (eng-sre): Also consider adaptive policy: start FIFO but switch to LFU/LRU for keys above a reuse threshold or for tenant types flagged as long-context. We'll need to track per-tenant reuse histograms.

Lina (eng-runtime): I'll open an issue with reproducer, logs, and the A/B data and schedule a follow-up hacking session. Ping me if you want in. Issue: https://redwood-internal/infra/issue/RI-evict-2026 (will add details). :memo:
